<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fixes #55510. When the process that launched vLLM dies without shutting it down (SIGKILL, OOM kill, crash), `EngineCore` and its TP workers keep running and hold the GPUs. A restart then fails the KV-cache memory check or OOMs.

Workers already exit when their parent dies, through the death pipe that `MultiprocExecutor` gives them. But their parent is `EngineCore`, and nothing tells `EngineCore` that its own parent is gone. This PR gives `EngineCore` the same death pipe, following @njhill's suggestion on #34816 ("set the shutdown flag and then kill after some delay"). On EOF the engine sends `ENGINE_CORE_DEAD` to its clients, aborts in-flight requests and runs the normal teardown, and force-kills its process tree if it is still alive 15 s later. The worker's monitor thread moves into a shared helper, `monitor_parent_death()`. Nothing changes while the parent is alive. If the parent dies during a SIGTERM drain, the engine switches to abort, since nothing is left to bound the drain.

Earlier attempts (#21915, #27686, #36055, #34816) were closed without being merged, and draft #40935 has been inactive since April.

## Validation

2× A100 80GB PCIe, torch 2.14.0+cu132, base `3dc6def360`. Reproducer: start `vllm serve hmellor/tiny-random-LlamaForCausalLM --enforce-eager`, `kill -9` the launcher, then check `ps` and `nvidia-smi`.

| Scenario | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| TP=2, kill the API server | EngineCore + 2 workers alive after 60 s, 150,790 MiB held | all exited after 8 s, 0 MiB |
| DP=2, kill the launcher | engines, workers and both API servers keep running, 150,362 MiB held | engines exited after 7 s, 0 MiB; both API servers got `EngineDeadError` and shut down (the CPU-only DP coordinator stays) |
| TP=2, kill during model load | EngineCore finishes loading, starts its workers and holds 150,790 MiB | all exited within 1 s, 0 MiB |

The 15 s force-kill never fired in these runs. @vinitrbl also confirmed `vllm run-batch` ([review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55846#pullrequestreview-5424839487)).

```
pytest tests/v1/engine/test_startup_watch_processes.py                       # 22 passed
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 pytest -v -s tests/v1/shutdown/test_parent_death.py # 2 passed (TP=1, TP=2)
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 pytest -v -s tests/v1/shutdown/test_delete.py tests/v1/shutdown/test_forward_error.py tests/v1/shutdown/test_startup_error.py  # 18 passed, 4 skipped
pytest -v -s tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_shutdown.py                    # 8 passed
```

On `main`, `test_parent_death.py` fails for both TP sizes because EngineCore and its workers outlive the parent, and the new `parent_exited` unit cases fail too. `pre-commit run --hook-stage manual` passes. ROCm and Intel XPU were not tested.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the patch, the tests and this description. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

Windows portability feedback for PR55846 (head73ce1bfbd82b12fd60e7a86cd182e36b7404dac8):

The new on_parent_death fallback uses `os.kill(os.getpid(), signal.SIGKILL)`. Windows Python has no SIGKILL, so if tree cleanup raises before killing self, the final fallback raises AttributeError too. The new shutdown test uses SIGKILL directly as well.

In CPU-only native Windows spawn fixtures using the exact PR monitor/callback functions, EOF detection worked after TerminateProcess of the parent. The unadapted early-init kill path raised AttributeError and left the child/test port alive; substituting SystemPanic's existing Windows-adapted kill_process_tree made it exit. A fake initialized engine's cooperative queue path also exited. These are mechanism tests, not real EngineCore/GPU/TP acceptance.

Could the last-resort self-exit use `os._exit(1)` after tree cleanup fails, avoiding POSIX-only signal constants, with a test injecting a tree-cleanup exception? This would make self-exit portable; it does not by itself prove worker-tree cleanup. A Windows test variant would also need Process.kill()/TerminateProcess semantics.

Gave this a try with `vllm run-batch`, since it isn't in the table and it's a slightly worse case: run-batch has no SIGTERM handler, so even a normal SIGTERM kills the launcher without telling the engine.

A10G, tiny random-weight Llama, 4000-request batch, signal sent to the run-batch process once a few hundred requests had finished. Base is main at the merge base (7867d6c), PR head 81aa514, both with `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1`.

| signal | main @ 7867d6c | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| SIGTERM | EngineCore still up after 60s, 21 GB held | gone, GPU free within 5s |
| SIGKILL | | gone, GPU free within 5s |

Both PR runs log `EngineCore: parent process exited, shutting down`. I didn't redo SIGKILL on 7867d6c, but on another main-based build (the #52505 branch) it orphaned the engine the same way.

On main the next run on the same GPU fails in `request_memory` until you kill the orphan by hand, so this is a nice fix for anyone retrying interrupted batch jobs. Might be worth adding run-batch to the list of covered cases.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Test that EngineCore and its workers exit when their parent process dies
+without shutting them down (API server SIGKILLed, OOM-killed or crashed)."""
+
+import contextlib
+import multiprocessing
+import os
+import signal
+import time
+
+import psutil
+import pytest
+
+from tests.utils import wait_for_gpu_memory_to_clear
+from tests.v1.shutdown.utils import (
+    SHUTDOWN_TEST_THRESHOLD_BYTES,
+    SHUTDOWN_TEST_TIMEOUT_SEC,
+)
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+from vllm.v1.engine.core import PARENT_DEATH_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_S
+
+MODELS = ["hmellor/tiny-random-LlamaForCausalLM"]
+
+# Cooperative shutdown budget plus a margin for the force-kill fallback.
+ORPHAN_EXIT_TIMEOUT_SEC = PARENT_DEATH_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_S + 30
+
+
+def _serve_until_killed(model: str, tensor_parallel_size: int, conn) -> None:
+    """Child process: start an LLM, report its engine process tree, then idle
+    until the test kills this process."""
+    from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams
+
+    llm = LLM(
+        model=model,
+        enforce_eager=True,
+        tensor_parallel_size=tensor_parallel_size,
+    )
+    llm.generate("Hello my name is", SamplingParams(max_tokens=1))
+    conn.send([child.pid for child in psutil.Process().children(recursive=True)])
+    conn.close()
+    while True:
+        time.sleep(1)
+
+
+def _is_running(pid: int) -> bool:
+    try:
+        return psutil.Process(pid).status() != psutil.STATUS_ZOMBIE
+    except psutil.NoSuchProcess:
+        return False
+
+
+def _wait_until_gone(pids: list[int], timeout: float) -> list[int]:
+    """Return the pids still running after ``timeout`` seconds."""
+    deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
+    while True:
+        alive = [pid for pid in pids if _is_running(pid)]
+        if not alive or time.monotonic() >= deadline:
+            return alive
+        time.sleep(0.5)
+
+
+def _kill_all(pids: list[int]) -> None:
+    for pid in pids:
+        with contextlib.suppress(ProcessLookupError):
+            os.kill(pid, signal.SIGKILL)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.timeout(SHUTDOWN_TEST_TIMEOUT_SEC * 2)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("model", MODELS)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("tensor_parallel_size", [2, 1])
+def test_engine_exits_after_parent_sigkill(model: str, tensor_parallel_size: int):
+    """SIGKILL the process that owns a running LLM; EngineCore and every
+    worker must exit on their own and release GPU memory."""
+    if current_platform.device_count() < tensor_parallel_size:
+        pytest.skip(reason="Not enough CUDA devices")
+
+    ctx = multiprocessing.get_context("spawn")
+    parent_conn, child_conn = ctx.Pipe(duplex=False)
+    proc = ctx.Process(
+        target=_serve_until_killed, args=(model, tensor_parallel_size, child_conn)
+    )
+    proc.start()
+    child_conn.close()
+    assert proc.pid is not None
+    parent_pid = proc.pid
+    engine_pids: list[int] = []
+    try:
+        assert parent_conn.poll(SHUTDOWN_TEST_TIMEOUT_SEC), "LLM did not start"
+        engine_pids = parent_conn.recv()
+        # EngineCore, plus one worker per rank when TP > 1.
+        expected = 1 + (tensor_parallel_size if tensor_parallel_size > 1 else 0)
+        assert len(engine_pids) >= expected, engine_pids
+        assert all(_is_running(pid) for pid in engine_pids)
+
+        os.kill(parent_pid, signal.SIGKILL)
+        proc.join(10)
+        assert proc.exitcode == -signal.SIGKILL
+
+        orphans = _wait_until_gone(engine_pids, ORPHAN_EXIT_TIMEOUT_SEC)
+        assert not orphans, f"engine processes outlived their parent: {orphans}"
+    finally:
+        if proc.is_alive():
+            proc.kill()
+        _kill_all(engine_pids)
+
+    wait_for_gpu_memory_to_clear(
+        devices=list(range(tensor_parallel_size)),
+        threshold_bytes=SHUTDOWN_TEST_THRESHOLD_BYTES,
+    )

+def monitor_parent_death(
+    death_pipe: Connection | None,
+    on_parent_death: Callable[[], None],
+    *,
+    name: str = "DeathPipeMonitor",
+) -> None:
+    """Run ``on_parent_death`` on a daemon thread once ``death_pipe`` hits EOF.
+
+    The parent keeps the write end open and never writes to it; the kernel
+    closes it when the parent exits by any means, including SIGKILL. Children
+    started with fork must close every inherited copy of the write end,
+    including their own.
+    """
+    if death_pipe is None:
+        return
+
+    def death_pipe_monitor():
+        try:
+            # This will block until parent process exits (pipe closes)
+            death_pipe.recv()
+        except EOFError:
+            on_parent_death()
+        except Exception as e:
+            logger.warning("Death monitoring error: %s", e)
+
+    threading.Thread(target=death_pipe_monitor, daemon=True, name=name).start()
+

@@ -1430,9 +1438,44 @@ def run_engine_core(*args, dp_rank: int = 0, local_dp_rank: int = 0, **kwargs):
         # Ensure we can serialize transformer config after spawning
         maybe_register_config_serialize_by_value()
 
+        death_pipe = kwargs.pop("death_pipe", None)
+        # Close write ends of death pipes inherited under fork.
+        for fd in kwargs.pop("inherited_fds", []):
+            try:
+                os.close(fd)
+            except OSError as e:

+                engine_core.output_queue.put_nowait(EngineCoreProc.ENGINE_CORE_DEAD)
+                time.sleep(PARENT_DEATH_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_S)
+                logger.warning(
+                    "[shutdown] EngineCore: still alive %ss after parent death, "
+                    "force-killing process tree",
+                    PARENT_DEATH_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_S,

+            except Exception:
+                logger.exception("[shutdown] EngineCore: force-kill failed")
+            finally:
+                # Only reached if kill_process_tree raised before killing us.
+                os._exit(1)
+
+        monitor_parent_death(death_pipe, on_parent_death, name="EngineCoreDeathMonitor")
         try:
             parallel_config: ParallelConfig = vllm_config.parallel_config

Windows portability feedback for PR55846 (head73ce1bfbd82b12fd60e7a86cd182e36b7404dac8):

The new on_parent_death fallback uses `os.kill(os.getpid(), signal.SIGKILL)`. Windows Python has no SIGKILL, so if tree cleanup raises before killing self, the final fallback raises AttributeError too. The new shutdown test uses SIGKILL directly as well.

In CPU-only native Windows spawn fixtures using the exact PR monitor/callback functions, EOF detection worked after TerminateProcess of the parent. The unadapted early-init kill path raised AttributeError and left the child/test port alive; substituting SystemPanic's existing Windows-adapted kill_process_tree made it exit. A fake initialized engine's cooperative queue path also exited. These are mechanism tests, not real EngineCore/GPU/TP acceptance.

Could the last-resort self-exit use `os._exit(1)` after tree cleanup fails, avoiding POSIX-only signal constants, with a test injecting a tree-cleanup exception? This would make self-exit portable; it does not by itself prove worker-tree cleanup. A Windows test variant would also need Process.kill()/TerminateProcess semantics.

AI assistance was used for investigation, fixtures and drafting. I have personally reviewed this draft.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Gave this a try with `vllm run-batch`, since it isn't in the table and it's a slightly worse case: run-batch has no SIGTERM handler, so even a normal SIGTERM kills the launcher without telling the engine.

A10G, tiny random-weight Llama, 4000-request batch, signal sent to the run-batch process once a few hundred requests had finished. Base is main at the merge base (7867d6c), PR head 81aa514, both with `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1`.

| signal | main @ 7867d6c | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| SIGTERM | EngineCore still up after 60s, 21 GB held | gone, GPU free within 5s |
| SIGKILL | | gone, GPU free within 5s |

Both PR runs log `EngineCore: parent process exited, shutting down`. I didn't redo SIGKILL on 7867d6c, but on another main-based build (the #52505 branch) it orphaned the engine the same way.

On main the next run on the same GPU fails in `request_memory` until you kill the orphan by hand, so this is a nice fix for anyone retrying interrupted batch jobs. Might be worth adding run-batch to the list of covered cases.
